reason: While the text does mention sacrifice as part of God's plan (instructing Moses to tell Pharaoh that the Israelites will 'sacrifice to the LORD our God' after three days' journey into the wilderness), the dominant emphasis throughout the passage is on God's compassion for His people's suffering in Egypt and His commitment to deliver them to a promised land. God's speeches focus on His awareness of the people's affliction ('I have surely seen the affliction of my people') and His purpose to bring them out to 'a good and broad land, flowing with milk and honey.' The sacrifice is mentioned as a stated purpose but is presented as secondary to the primary divine concerns of liberation and covenant fulfillment. The text does not position proper worship and sacrifice as what is fundamentally important to Yahweh, but rather emphasizes divine mercy and deliverance.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
